name: read-requirements-derived-realised-by
description: A set-valued computed value on the requirements layer: `derived: ["realised_by"]` adds to each requirement one row per `satisfies` member naming it, across the five link-carrying layers, as `{"layer", "element", "member", "kind", "stated"}` — `member` the port or runnable holding the link and `null` for an element's own list, `kind` one of the seven site kinds (`swc`, `port`, `runnable`, `interface`, `composition`, `task`, or a hardware element's own kind), `stated` the version the link states and `null` for a bare id or a malformed suffix. The sites are the ones the trace rules read, enumerated over the loaded state in the contract's layer order, then element order, then file order; an element-form member names no requirement and is no site. A requirement nothing realises has no row: `allocation` (`{"sites", "elements", "allocated"}`, one row per requirement) answers which requirements are unallocated, and `stale_links` which links need confirming.

context.summary: The base model, whose two components each name `REQ_EXAMPLE_001@1` in their own `satisfies`, with a bare `REQ_EXAMPLE_001` on `ExampleConsumerSWC`'s port `rIn`, `REQ_EXAMPLE_001@1` on the interface `IExample`, and a second requirement, `REQ_EXAMPLE_002`, that nothing names. So `REQ_EXAMPLE_001` answers four rows — two components, a port and an interface — and `REQ_EXAMPLE_002` none.
context.notes: A read takes no scope and writes no audit record.

expected.notes: `REQ_EXAMPLE_002` has no row: a set-valued computed value drops the row it has no value for, so "which requirements does nothing realise" is `derived: ["allocation"]` with `where: [{"field": "derived.allocation.allocated", "equals": false}]`, never the index minus these rows. The three requirement values apply at the elements of the `requirements` layer alone: asked at another layer or at a member path they are `schema-violation`, never a blank.
